Here’s a quick‑look at the **long weekends** that Canadians will enjoy in 2023 (based on the federal holidays that create a three‑day break).  
(If you’re looking for provincial‑specific holidays—e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in NL, Family Day in BC, etc.—you’ll need to add those separately.)

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Day of Week | Long‑Weekend Span |
|---------|-------------|-------------|-------------------|
| New Year’s Day (observed) | Jan 2 | Mon | Sat Dec 31 – Mon Jan 2 |
| Family Day (Ontario, Manitoba, NB, PEI, Saskatchewan) | Feb 20 | Mon | Fri Feb 17 – Mon Feb 20 |
| Good Friday | Apr 7 | Fri | Fri Apr 7 – Sun Apr 9 |
| Victoria Day | May 22 | Mon | Fri May 19 – Mon May 22 |
| Canada Day (observed) | Jul 3 | Mon | Sat Jul 1 – Mon Jul 3 |
| Civic Holiday (most provinces) | Aug 7 | Mon | Fri Aug 4 – Mon Aug 7 |
| Labour Day | Sep 4 | Mon | Fri Sep 1 – Mon Sep 4 |
| Thanksgiving | Oct 9 | Mon | Fri Oct 6 – Mon Oct 9 |
| Christmas Day | Dec 25 | Mon | Fri Dec 22 – Mon Dec 25 |

> **Quick notes**  
> • “Observed” means the holiday falls on a weekend and the next weekday is treated as the official holiday.  
> • These are the *federal* holidays that create a three‑day break. Provincial holidays may add more long weekends (e.g., St. Patricks’ Day in NL on Mar 17, Family Day in BC on Feb 20, etc.).  

Feel free to plug this table into your holiday‑planning app!
